title: Woke up to 10GB of motion study data (Videos, Images, and Metadata)
author: Fun-City-9820
selftext:
It looks like my agents have been experimenting all night with motion and animations. I have 10gb+ worth of videos and images of studies done by my agents to improve motion and animation for our upcoming game

Thought id share

comments.author: remorej
comments.body: Those movements are awesome. Is that automatic during gameplay or carefully crafted by the model at design-time?

replies.author: Fun-City-9820
replies.body: This is all gameplay! Theres far more but this was just one of many concepts it came up with using the actual gameplay in a sandbox

comments.author: FondantIcy866
comments.body: Cool! How did you set this up?

replies.author: Fun-City-9820
replies.body:
Thanks! I’m using **T3 Code** with **Codex** and **Claude Code** agents working on different parts of our **Godot** project.

Basically, I give them a specific motion-study task—like entering a ship, taking off, or comparing chase and cockpit cameras. They inspect the existing assets/code, build an isolated review scene, script the movement, and render it in Godot. **Python/PowerShell** handles the batch runs, then **FFmpeg** turns the captures into MP4s and extracts frames for review.

They save the scene scripts, videos, images and motion metadata together so we can inspect what happened, revise it, and render again. It took multiple tasks and iterations rather than one magic prompt.

These are concept studies with scripted movement, not finished gameplay. I still review the results and choose what gets integrated and tested. That separation lets us explore a lot without changing the actual game every time.

replies.author: FondantIcy866
replies.body: Cool! What's the usage cost like? I am wondering if it's worth paying for dedicated animation AI or just using part of my claude ultra sub to do this each week.

replies.author: Fun-City-9820
replies.body:
I run this nightly and spend about 7h reviewing the videos, images, data and letting the agent know the changes i want and what to implement into the game and how. To me its worth it, but I do have a sub for both Claude and ChatGPT.

Below is what it would have cost me via API whenever I needed this. I'll get a breakdown by features implemented shortly to give you a better sense. What I do are large iteration cycles so this may be excessive so some

replies.author: Brave-History-6502
replies.body: That seems super expensive -- thats like a quarter of a week of usage for small animation tweaks. There def has to be a better way!

replies.author: Fun-City-9820
replies.body: The video i posted was juat one of many. It animated over 50 items, updated modeling , graphics, adeudo animations,  effects, synthesized new sounds and audio as well as a bunch of physics logic. I dont think alot of people do this level of commits a day (2k). What i do is basically ask to see how a player could walk 10 different ways, but for a bunch of different things then pick out the best. This obviously will get expensive but its how I get to see new things as well as pick the best
